claims.text: Simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature produce accelerated coupled degradation in a multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy.
Micro-galvanic coupling between the alloy phases is the primary cause of the accelerated coupled degradation.
Multiple phases in the eutectic high-entropy alloy enable micro-galvanic coupling.
Micro-galvanic coupling between phases causes selective dissolution of certain phases.
The selectively dissolved phase can be a body-centered-cubic or B2 phase.
Elevated-temperature wear promotes formation of an oxide layer.
Total degradation of the multi-phase alloy will be significantly higher than that of a single-phase alloy or an alloy without micro-galvanic coupling.
A comparison with a single-phase alloy or an alloy without micro-galvanic coupling can isolate the effect of micro-galvanic coupling.
Temperature range and the presence of specific phases define the relevant operating boundary.
Alloy composition, processing history, and environmental conditions may influence degradation behavior.

contradictions.description: The mechanism invokes formation of a protective oxide layer, while the predicted outcome is accelerated degradation. No explanation is given for why the selective-dissolution contribution outweighs the oxide layer's protective effect; the cited wear evidence instead associates the oxide with increased wear resistance.
